title: Ruby on Rails
body:
An opinionated server-side web framework written in Ruby, organised around [[MVC]] and the principle of convention over configuration: follow the standard layout and a great deal of wiring is free. A fully-equipped kitchen with a standard layout, so any trained chef knows where the knives are.

The pieces: **routes** map URL + [[HTTP Verb]] to a controller action; the **controller** receives the parsed request, calls the model, and hands off to the view; the **model** holds data and business rules, backed by [[ActiveRecord]]; the **view** renders HTML or [[JSON]]. Schema changes are managed with [[Database Migration]]s. Every one of these runs on the server — none of it reaches the browser. Rails predates the async server era, so unlike [[Node.js]] its default request handling is blocking, which is why Rails apps scale by running many worker processes.
